title: 2018_PMC6013082_Strategic_Response_to_an_Outbreak_of_Circulating_Vaccine-Derived
ehr_evidence: The report relies on polio surveillance data rather than electronic health records; as stated, 'The vaccination status of patients aged 6–59 months with nonpolio AFP (NPAFP) can be used as a proxy for OPV vaccination coverage' and cases were identified through acute flaccid paralysis (AFP) surveillance and stool specimen testing.
summary: This MMWR outbreak report describes the epidemiology and public health response to a circulating vaccine-derived poliovirus type 2 (cVDPV2) outbreak in Syria (2017–2018), identifying 74 cases and reporting that intensified AFP surveillance, environmental sewage sampling, and three rounds of mOPV2 vaccination campaigns interrupted transmission.
key_findings: 74 cVDPV2 cases were identified with the most recent case in September 2017; 46 (62%) occurred in females.
The median patient age was 15 months, with 26 (35%) aged <12 months, 35 (47%) aged 12–23 months, 11 (15%) aged 24–59 months, and 2 (3%) aged ≥5 years.
71 (96%) of 74 cases were reported from Deir-ez-Zor governorate (58 from Mayadeen district, 12 from Boukamal district, 1 from Deir-ez-Zor district).
30 cases (41%) had never received a dose of OPV, 32 (43%) received 1–2 doses, and 12 (16%) received ≥3 OPV doses.

Administrative mOPV2 coverage in Deir-ez-Zor was ~79% (postcampaign monitoring recall 88%) in the first campaign and 77% in the second; in Raqqa, administrative coverage was 86% then 114% with postcampaign monitoring of 57% and 84% respectively.
Enhanced surveillance coupled with mOPV2 vaccination successfully interrupted cVDPV2 transmission in Syria.
captured_features: cVDPV2 case counts by governorate and month of paralysis onset
stool specimen adequacy and AFP surveillance rates
administrative vaccination coverage and postcampaign monitoring (recall) coverage
genomic sequence differences from Sabin vaccine virus (22 nucleotides in VP1)
population: Children in Syria, particularly those aged <5 years (median 15 months) in Deir-ez-Zor governorate, during the 2017–2018 cVDPV2 outbreak
exposure_domain: vaccination (OPV/mOPV2 coverage) and low routine immunization coverage
limitations: Administrative vaccination coverage denominators may not reflect the actual target population because of frequent population movement to and from the outbreak-affected area.
Delays in receiving laboratory results due to difficulties transporting stool specimens during the humanitarian emergency.
Subnational gaps in AFP surveillance performance limited earlier detection of the outbreak.
